events_chronological: A young man grows up in a small provincial town on the continent and qualifies in medicine.
He marries, and the child born to the couple dies as an infant.
He takes a post at an institute where the disabled are put to death by injection and by gas.
He is posted to a camp in the east and stands beside the senior physician during selections on the platform.
Inside the camp he performs dental procedures and experiments on the prisoners.
He takes a prisoner as a mistress and sends her to the chamber once he has tired of her.
The camp is cleared before the advancing army arrives and he walks west with forged papers in his coat.
He spends years in hiding on the southern coast under an assumed name, living quietly on gold.
He crosses the ocean under a second false name, given fresh papers by a clergyman who asks him nothing.
Working in hospitals abroad, he inflicts pain on his patients and persuades himself that he is curing them.
He carries on a long affair with a woman who never learns a single true thing about him.
He grows old under a third name, gardening, hoarding tinned food, and waking from dreams of a man in a white coat.
He collapses among his flowerbeds and dies in a hospital far from where he began.
nonlinear_category_reason: Scene order runs from the latest stretch to the earliest throughout, with no present-day level the telling returns to. A narrator riding inside a doctor's body experiences the life from death to birth, so the whole of it is told in reverse.
syuzhet_notes: The narration runs strictly from the death back to the birth, so the doctor looks like a healer and the camp looks like a place where people are assembled. The first told bullet is the last thing that happens and the last bullet the first.
fabula_notes: Because the narrating voice reads every action in reverse, the surface of the prose inverts cause and effect. These bullets record what actually happened, in the order it happened.
